titulo: Live background: video generated inside the site
lead: A long opening film comes from several short clips chained together, each starting on the last real frame of the one before. The risk is a hidden cut in the middle of a clip. The site-movimento skill has gates that catch it. You run them on rehearsal clips, one continuous and one with a cut, without spending credits.
objetivo: chain clips into a continuous film and prove with the site-movimento gates that there is no hidden cut.

aprende.t: The seven steps of the site-movimento skill and where the gates come in
The engine contract (Kling, Agnes, Kie, your own) tested without spending, with DRY_RUN
Assemble the film and prove continuity; catch the hidden cut
The copy gate in Portuguese, English, and Spanish

hero_alt: Wide monitor in a dark room showing a page whose background is a mountain landscape with mist at dawn.

secoes.sub: Step 4 of the skill (video). Click each stage.

nos.detalhe: Chained key images, one small camera step at a time. A step that's too big makes the generator cut to get there. vetor.py checks the direction of the prompts before spending.
Every engine follows the same contract: start, end, prompt, seconds, output. Clip 2 starts on the REAL last frame of clip 1 (extracted pixels, never the keyframe). In order, never in parallel.

fixacao.py: did the engine respect the start frame and the end frame? cortes.py: is there a hidden cut in the middle? A clip with a cut never goes in: bring the keyframes closer together and redo it. Don't hide it with a fade.
Joins the clips (from the 2nd on, starting at frame 1, because frame 0 repeats the last one of the previous clip), writes film/master.mp4, extracts all the frames, and the manifest.json.
continuidade.py compares each pair of frames against the LOCAL median: smooth motion passes even when fast; a cut is a sudden drop; frozen is a dead zone in the scroll. PASSA = one single movement.

secoes.volta: cut? bring them closer and redo
secoes.legenda: Without a video engine, the skill makes the film in code (steps 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7 are the same). Pilot numbers: 300 Kling 3.0 credits at 720p, 285 frames in the horizontal film and 361 in the vertical one (README, 10/18/2026).

secoes.sub: With DRY_RUN=1 each engine only shows what it would do. The test checks all four.

secoes.titulo: Two chained clips become the site's film
secoes.sub: The rehearsal imitates the chaining: clip 2 starts at the zoom where clip 1 ended.

blocos.rot: Terminal · chain, assemble, and prove continuity
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cARCKHÉ-ia-sites-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-sites/a6; SM=$E/site-movimento/skill/site-movimento/scripts
# dois clipes encadeados: o 2º começa exatamente onde o 1º terminou (zoom 1,25)
bash "$K/scripts/clipe.sh" "$K/exemplos/lente.jpg" "$E/c1.mp4" 4 1.0 1.25
bash "$K/scripts/clipe.sh" "$K/exemplos/lente.jpg" "$E/c2.mp4" 4 1.25 1.5
python3 "$SM/cortes.py" "$E/c1.mp4" "$E/c2.mp4" | sed "s#$E/##"; echo "cortes: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
rm -rf "$E/site"; cp -r "$K/site" "$E/site"
python3 "$SM/montar.py" "$E/site" "$E/c1.mp4:0:-1" "$E/c2.mp4:1:-1" | head -1 | sed "s#$E/##"
python3 "$SM/continuidade.py" "$E/site/frames" | sed "s#$E/##"; echo "saída: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

4 s + 4 s = 191 frames (frame 0 of clip 2 is dropped so it isn't repeated). montar.py writes to site/frames, the folder the kit page already reads.

secoes.sub: A clip that jumps scenes in the middle: the lens in the dark studio and, suddenly, on the light background.

blocos.rot: Terminal · a clip with a cut
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cARCKHÉ-ia-sites-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-sites/a6; SM=$E/site-movimento/skill/site-movimento/scripts
# a clip with a hidden cut in the middle: the lens in the dark studio and, suddenly, on the light background
bash "$K/scripts/clipe.sh" "$K/exemplos/lente.jpg" "$E/a.mp4" 2 1.0 1.1
bash "$K/scripts/clipe.sh" "$K/exemplos/lente-clara.jpg" "$E/b.mp4" 2 1.1 1.2
ffmpeg -v error -y -i "$E/a.mp4" -i "$E/b.mp4" -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]concat=n=2:v=1[v]" -map "[v]" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 "$E/c3.mp4"
python3 "$SM/cortes.py" "$E/c3.mp4" | sed "s#$E/##"; echo "saída: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

abas.html:
a.mp4: 2,0 s · 24 fps · 1920×1080
b.mp4: 2,0 s · 24 fps · 1920×1080
c3.mp4 quadros 97, mediana 1.00, piores [(48, 0.46), (72, 0.99)] CORTE no(s) quadro(s) [48]
saída: 1

The frame pair at 48 drops to 0.46 against a median of 1.00: a cut. A cut between two dark, similar frames can slip past cortes.py; that's why the skill also runs continuidade.py and you watch the film.

secoes.sub: Paid clips go out in order, one at a time. Run it, interrupt it, and run it again: only what's missing comes back.

msg.inicio: 5 steps in fila/. Click "Run the queue".
msg.rodando: One step at a time: the next clip depends on the real last frame of the previous one.
msg.parou: Interrupted. The middle step stayed in rodando/. Run again to see the resume.
msg.retoma: Resume: what was in rodando/ went back to the queue. A clip that's already done isn't generated again (or charged again).
msg.fim: Queue empty: clips, assembly, and continuity done.
msg.fimfalha: Queue empty. Clip 3 went to falhou/ (hidden cut): bring the keyframes closer and redo only that one.

secoes.legenda: Simulation in the browser: nothing is generated. The failure is on purpose, to show that only the clip with the cut comes back.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

opcoes: From the keyframe you approved for the end of clip 1, without changing anything.
From the last real frame of clip 1, extracted from the video.
From the first frame of clip 1.
perguntas.explica: The engine never ends exactly on the keyframe. Starting from the last real frame (extracted pixels) makes the seam match by construction.

perguntas.p: cortes.py found a cut in the middle of clip 3. What does the skill tell you to do?
opcoes: Hide the cut with a fade.
Bring the keyframes closer together and redo clip 3.
Buy a bridge clip that leads from one side of the cut to the other.
Move on: nobody notices it while scrolling.
perguntas.explica: The person stops scrolling exactly at the cut. A fade or a flash draws attention; a bridge cuts again. Use a smaller camera step and redo it.

perguntas.p: Why does continuidade.py compare against the local median instead of a fixed threshold?
opcoes: Because a fast, smooth tracking shot scores low and a cut between similar frames scores high; the shape of the curve tells the two apart.
Because the fixed threshold is slow.
Because each generator uses a different scale.
Because ffmpeg does not compute SSIM.
perguntas.explica: Smooth motion: each pair looks like its neighbors, however low the score. Cut: a sharp drop below the median of its neighbors. That is what the script itself explains in its header.

perguntas.p: What does DRY_RUN=1 guarantee in the engine test?
opcoes: That the clip comes out cheaper.
That the engine uses the test key.
That the video is generated at low resolution.
That no service is called: the engine only shows the command.
perguntas.explica: The script exits before reading a key or calling the network. It is the way to test the contract without spending anything.

itens.texto: Clip N starts on the last real frame of the previous one, in order.
pinning, cuts, continuity; a cut never gets in.
DRY_RUN and rehearsal clips prove the path before the generator.
